Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) General Dhiraj Seth. File | Photo Credit: PTI
Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) General Dhiraj Seth on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) visited Mana and Joshimath in the Garhwal Sector to review the Army’s operational preparedness and assess initiatives aimed at developing border areas and empowering local communities.
During the visit, General Seth was briefed on operational readiness, combat preparedness and ongoing infrastructure development projects in the sector. Interacting with troops, he commended their professionalism, dedication and resilience in safeguarding the country’s frontiers, the Army said.
Emphasising the need to remain prepared for evolving security challenges, the Army Chief called for greater integration of technology, continuous capability enhancement and sustained operational vigilance.
As part of the Army’s efforts to strengthen border communities and promote sustainable livelihoods, General Seth also visited Mana, recognised as India’s First Village. He appreciated the efforts of Army personnel and local residents in promoting tourism, preserving the region’s cultural heritage and creating opportunities for socio-economic development.
The visit underscored the Army’s dual focus on maintaining operational readiness along the borders and contributing to the development of remote border villages.
